= Local Rustls client-certificate request adapter

This directory contains the published Rustls 0.23.46 source from the local Cargo registry source cache.
The upstream package is https://crates.io/crates/rustls/0.23.46[Rustls 0.23.46] and its repository is https://github.com/rustls/rustls[rustls/rustls].
`UPSTREAM.sha256` records the original contents of every copied source, manifest, build script, example, benchmark, README, and license before local changes.
The manifest SHA-256 is `0357340433a76253e46bed7ab1e5b1b6efed92a89e7515e583fb9af6b2759c9c`.
The source cache did not contain an archive checksum; the manifest identifies the available source without asserting an independently verified release archive.
The Apache-2.0, ISC, and MIT licenses are retained alongside the source.

The workspace patches the crates.io package so direct Kafka, reqwest, and tokio-rustls consumers use one Rustls crate identity.
The local adapter adds `client::ClientCertificateRequest` and the defaulted `ResolvesClientCert::resolve_with_request` method.
The borrowed request exposes the peer's certificate signature preferences separately from its protocol-compatible CertificateVerify schemes, and preserves TLS 1.2 certificate-type bytes.
TLS 1.3 parses `signature_algorithms_cert` and falls back to the unfiltered `signature_algorithms` list when the former is absent.
Existing resolvers receive the same protocol-compatible schemes through the default adapter.
CertificateRequest serialization and parsing reject duplicate or empty certificate signature lists.

The request view is passive and borrows the current handshake only for resolver invocation.
It adds no independently scheduled work or retained connection state.
TLS 1.2 temporarily maps the at-most-255 certificate-type enum values to wire bytes during that invocation.
The common resolver still requires a key capable of producing a CertificateVerify signature from the protocol-compatible scheme list.

Source audit covers every workspace client and resolver, Rustls's built-in resolvers, and reqwest 0.13.4's client identity and preconfigured-client paths.
Kafka's Registry client is the workspace's only custom client-certificate resolver.
The pgwire, pg-source, and server consumers retain their existing default resolver behavior.
The published Cargo package omits upstream `src/testdata` and integration-test assets; those omissions are unchanged.
Focused request parser and resolver adapter regression sources are included in the existing unit-test modules.
Builds and test execution remain subject to the repository's source-completeness gate.
